## Shared scenes

> The Ashdown children find a runaway girl named [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) hiding in an old barn near their home. They feed her and listen as she shares her tragic past, her escape from her abusive guardian, and her unique perspectives on life and religion.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P4](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0004), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P27](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0027), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P35](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0035)_

> Mary discusses her fear of damnation and beatings with [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) and [Grace](../character/grace.md) before being introduced to the [Carrows](../codex/factions.md#carrows) at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow). Afterwards, the girls arrange for Mary to sleep in the parsonage garret room. Later that night, [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) comforts Mary in the garret, where Mary expresses her fears and jealousy before they reconcile and fall asleep.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P87](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0087), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P93](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0093), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P106](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0106), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P127](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0127)_

> [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) attends church with the manse children using borrowed clothes, making a scene by sticking her tongue out at a parishioner. Refusing to attend school, she cleans the manse, spars with [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) over food, and spends time with the local children at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow). Despite occasional arguments, Mary captivates the children with her stories, ghost tales, and unique tricks.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P8](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P9](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0009), [v5 CHAPTER VI. > Miss Winifred interrogates Mary at the manse and later updates [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) after learning that Mrs. [Grimble](../character/grimble.md) has died. Meanwhile, the children gather at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow), where Edmund reads myths and imagines the Pied Piper leading them away. [Bess](../character/bess-carrow.md) arrives with news of Mrs. Grimble's death, startling Mary, but [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) reassures her and promises to pray that Mary can remain in [Seven Gulls](../codex/places.md#seven-gulls).
>

> Miss Winifred urges Mr. Ashdown to address Mary's upbringing, leading Mr. Ashdown to speak warmly with the girl. Driven by Mary's impending return to the asylum, [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) visits Miss Winifred to ask if she will take Mary in. After consulting her husband [Ambrose](../character/ambrose.md), Miss Winifred agrees to adopt Mary, and the children give Mary farewell gifts.
>

> Mary and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) converse about faith and the possibility of Mr. Ashdown remarrying, which leaves [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) frightened and tearful. Meanwhile, [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) reads through the night and contemplates his late wife, oblivious to Ida's distress.
>

> While their father is away and [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) is bedridden, [Grace](../character/grace.md) and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) attempt to clean the house, but accidentally spark a village scandal when they beat carpets in the cemetery, believing it is Monday rather than Sunday.
>

> Mary informs [Grace](../character/grace.md) and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) that they caused a scandal in the community by doing household chores on Sunday after getting their days mixed up. [Grace](../character/grace.md) laughs off the mistake once she realizes how the days were miscounted, reassuring [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) that she has a plan to clarify everything to the town.
>

> Miss Winifred dismisses [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) after her knitting, and Mary runs to [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow) to share news with [Grace Ashdown](../character/grace.md) about [Kitty Hector](../character/twiss.md) and the Fairlies' threats to force Grace's father out. [Grace](../character/grace.md) despairs over the thought of having to leave the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen), but while looking out her bedroom window at night, she hatches a plan to visit [Lionel Fairlie](../character/lionel-fairlie.md) and fix the problem herself.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XV. MORE GOSSIP

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XV. MORE GOSSIP P33](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0033), [v5 CHAPTER XV. MORE GOSSIP P34](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0034), [v5 CHAPTER XV. > [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) joins [Grace](../character/grace.md), [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md), [Bess](../character/bess-carrow.md), and [Izzy](../character/izzy.md) in [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow) to chew spruce gum. [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) feels envious of Mary's fine new clothes and muff, while Mary brings news of local gossip and mentions that [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) killed a rooster for dinner. Horrified that their pet rooster [Adam](../character/adam.md) has been killed, [Grace](../character/grace.md) rushes home, prompting [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) to repentantly give Mary her gum and compliment her muff.
>

> After being teased at school about the loss of her rooster [Adam](../character/adam.md), [Grace](../character/grace.md) goes toward [Hollowmere](../codex/places.md#hollowmere) seeking comfort from Mrs. [Carrow](../character/carrow.md). In [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow), she meets [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md), who listens sympathetically to Grace's grief and offers her a pet canary. [Grace](../character/grace.md) returns home feeling comforted and tells her father and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) how much she loves [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md).
>

> [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) scolds the manse children in the graveyard for their misbehavior and the gossip it causes, revealing rumors that their father might marry [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md). After Mary leaves, [Kit Carrow](../character/kit-carrow.md) arrives and suggests they start a [Good-Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#good-conduct-club) to manage their behavior and avoid bringing shame on their father.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXIII. THE GOOD-CONDUCT CLUB

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XXIII. THE GOOD-CONDUCT CLUB P3](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0003), [v5 CHAPTER XXIII. THE GOOD-CONDUCT CLUB P33](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0033), [v5 CHAPTER XXIII. > At Kit's suggestion, [Grace](../character/grace.md) and her siblings decide to form the [Good-Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#good-conduct-club) to self-regulate their behavior and avoid bringing shame on their father. After writing up their agreement and signing it in the cemetery by lantern light, [Grace](../character/grace.md) and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) go to bed and discuss Mary Stubbs's warnings about stepmothers and the rumor about Miss Ainslie.
>

> [Grace](../character/grace.md) scandalizes the congregation by wearing boots without stockings to church, drawing sharp criticism from local gossips while [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) and the Carrow girls rush to her defense. To protect her father's reputation and fulfill a punishment imposed by Tobias, [Grace](../character/grace.md) publishes an explanatory letter in the local newspaper detailing why she gave away her last good stockings.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXV. ANOTHER SCANDAL AND ANOTHER “EXPLANATION”

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XXV. ANOTHER SCANDAL AND ANOTHER “EXPLANATION” P0](../source/v05-c25.md#nw-v05-c25-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER XXV. > The [Good-Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#good-conduct-club) decides to fast on Sunday as punishment for their graveyard song, which causes [Ida Ashdown](../character/ida-ashdown.md) to faint during the church service. Doctor [Hugh Carrow](../character/hugh-carrow.md) and Mrs. Elder Clow help revive her, leading [Grace](../character/grace.md) to explain their self-punishment rule to their distraught father. Realizing how neglected his children are, [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) reflects mournfully on his duties as a father and his unresolved love for [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) before returning to his theological studies.
>

> While spending a pleasant spring evening at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow), the children share their dreams for the future until [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) arrives and startles them with a ghost story about [Henry Warren](../character/henry-warren.md) and the nearby ruined [Bailey](../codex/places.md#bailey) property. After Mary cooks trout for the group, darkness falls and the lingering terror forces [Grace](../character/grace.md), [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md), and [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) to head home together, carefully avoiding the old garden.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE

> Tobias punishes [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) for running away from a ghost by forcing him to sit on a graveyard tombstone until midnight. [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) endures the chilly rain during his midnight vigil and subsequently falls gravely ill with double pneumonia. After a tense battle for his life, [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) recovers with the support of the community and returns to [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow).
>

> [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) gossip-shares village rumors with [Grace](../character/grace.md) and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) about why [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) refused their father's proposal and how [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) threw an eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy. Learning of the incident, Mr. Ashdown intends to whip [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) in his study, but relents at the last second when he sees his late wife's eyes in the boy, leaving both father and son deeply shaken.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXXIII. RUPERT IS—NOT—WHIPPED

> [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Miss Winifred discuss the upcoming marriages of [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) Ashdown and [Harriet Ainslie](../character/harriet-ainslie.md), as well as plans for the minister's children while he is away. Meanwhile, the local children gather outdoors on Kit's final night before leaving for Regent's [Academy](../codex/places.md#regent-s-academy), where Edmund imagines the Pied Piper calling the boys away to follow him.
>
